title: Diagnostics: pre-solve checks, IIS message, why-deferred report

blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: A Budget Lock scenario fixes a project to start in 2028, where it spends $9,000k in its one year of work, and finance locks 2028 at $8,000k. Nothing else changes. What reports the problem?

options.text: The deletion filter, once the solve has come back INFEASIBLE with no plan
options.says: The checks run first; a project fixed to a year counts as required, and a required project that fits no year alone is a check's finding, with no solver.

options.text: The quality gate of lesson 13.1.1, since it compares spend with budgets
options.says: The lesson says the gate reads only the portfolio, so it sees neither a scenario's overrides nor its locked numbers; here both matter.

options.text: The pre-solve checks, since a fixed project is required and fits nowhere
options.says: Right: overrides count as required, and alone-over-budget fires before any model is built.

options.text: Nothing at all, since an override is a bound the solver applies by itself
options.says: Overrides count in the checks; and an infeasible model is diagnosed, not left silent.

origin.section: Pre-Solve Checks Run First and Catch What One Limit Can Refuse

questions.stem: The milestone's deletion filter switches off budget, crew, floor, must-do and forced rows, but never the once, alternative and precedence rows. Why are those three families kept on?

options.text: Because nobody at Budget Lock can change them, so such a conflict helps no one
options.says: Right: "a project starts at most once" is not a number anyone at Budget Lock can change.

options.text: Because they never take part in a conflict, so testing them would only cost solves
options.says: The design note says a conflict made of once and precedence rows would be true, and useless: they can be in one.

options.text: Because the run setting's 0.1% gap leaves solves on those rows without a clear answer
options.says: The lesson says the run setting's gap plays no part in the filter: with no objective, each solve only finds a plan or proves there is none.

options.text: Because they hold the numbers this scenario changed, which the filter must not drop
options.says: The scenario changed only the 2028 budget and two transmission crew limits, which are budget and crew rows, and those the filter does switch off.

origin.section: A Deletion Filter Names the Rules That Clash

questions.stem: With the run setting, the base plan is worth $50,000k with bound $50,050k; with a deferred project forced in, the plan is worth $49,900k with bound $49,950k. What forcing cost does the report give?

options.text: Exactly $100k, the difference between the two plans' values
options.says: Neither plan value is exact under a gap; the report gives an interval, base plan minus forced bound to base bound minus forced plan.

options.text: Between $0k and $150k, since a forcing cost interval starts at zero
options.says: The low end is the base plan less the forced bound, here $50k, not zero.

options.text: Between $50k and $100k, since the bounds cut the difference from above
options.says: The high end is the base bound less the forced plan, $150k.

options.text: Between $50k and $150k, from the two plan values and the two bounds
